I helped Holly with After Hours Art Barn. I'm happy to take that over from her. This would be the traditional 3:30-5pm slots. 
Shondell Dahm was with us this year, and she's interested in offering "Make and Mingle" or something like that for Jr Teens, Sr Teens and all Adults during the 5-6:15 pm slot. This would be a safe place for adults to hang who maybe don't enjoy the social or drinking aspect of Happy Hour, but want to be with other similar souls.

For both After Hours Art Barn and Make and Mingle, ideally you would have 3 or 4 people total for the week, and then we could work amongst ourselves to make up a schedule for rotating.  

Also, once you have your theme for the Banquet solidified, let us know, so we can dream up table decorations for folks to do in the art barn connected to the banquet theme.

column6: My family struggled with the banquet this year. We signed up too late to reserve a table inside; and then the tables outside were really overcrowded. We could not hear much from inside b/c everyone on the porch was noisy. It ended up feeling like a regular dinner, only more stressful due to seating issues, and we felt kind of sad. And that was with good weather; it would have been miserable with bad weather.  I think if we are going to continue to have 300 conferees, then we need to have some conversations about how to re-envision banquet night. I am not sure the same processes/plans work with current conference needs and values. I felt like all the other meals worked fine with a large conference, but banquet was kind of a mess.

column5: I wonder if there could be something like a "spontaneity hour" (or two hours) plugged into the week. That is, a time that is not scheduled long in advance, but which people can announce on the second chalk board sort of special things they would like to try. Like a porch sing, a multi-generational trip to Betty Moody's cave, an ultimate frisbee game .. etc. Does that make sense?
column6:
1. Too much packed into first night -- lovely events do not get the attention they deserve (marshmallow roast; chapel; get acquainted). If there is no 15x20 next year, maybe an adaptation of get acquainted could be inserted into Monday night instead? 

2. Too much of our musical traditions turn on the willingness of Ray Castoldi to support everyone. My proposed solution would be to get a grant from ISAUU to bring in a designated accompanist to support all of the demands for a pianist  -- this would need to be arranged early, since so many folks are already getting started on their musical ideas in the winter and spring. 

3. Unclear whether there is enough for kids (pre-teens and teens) to do after the Grand March on Friday. 

4. I wonder if there could be a nudge toward more inclusiveness in practice over the week. In theory, we know that everyone is welcome to all events or to join any team/group. But could we be more explicit about encouraging inclusion of people who may not be well acquainted with the regular cast of characters? Without malice, our conference drifts toward cliquie-ness. I'd like to see that dialed back, to the extent possible.
column7: Farewell party! I learned a lot but do not necessarily want to do it again. I am not sure the traditional model of just assuming that our regular musicians will be up for playing is the best way. Or, maybe we should just accept the imperfections of an event which is almost certainly going to be anticlimactic.
